## Purpose

`backend/app/api/` is the FastAPI route layer: 27 modules of thin HTTP/SSE/WebSocket handlers
that authenticate/authorize a request, call into services/models/the agent runtime, and shape
a response.

**[app/main.py](../../backend/app/main.py) (`[MOD-backend-app](MOD-backend-app.md)`) mounts every router here and is the sole importer of this
package**; nothing in the kernel (`agents/execution_engine/`) or the deepagents runtime imports
back into app.api.

## Shape

The routers split into thematic clusters. The most structurally interesting is the
run-transport cluster (the SSE cutover, REQ-CHAT-07/D-13) sitting alongside the definitions-vs-
history split (D-02):

Auth & identity:

- [auth.py](../../backend/app/api/auth.py) -> `/api/auth`: register (403-disabled, invite-only), login, `GET /me`, logout,
  change-password.
- [api_key_auth.py](../../backend/app/api/api_key_auth.py) — no router; `get_user_via_api_key` FastAPI dependency resolving the
  `X-Flowin-API-Key` header (SHA-256 hash lookup against `UserApiKey`) for IDE/MCP clients that
  can't hold a 24h JWT.
- [admin.py](../../backend/app/api/admin.py) -> `/api/admin`: user list/create/delete + tier `PATCH`, gated on `is_admin=True`.
- [settings.py](../../backend/app/api/settings.py) -> `/api/settings`: GitHub PAT CRUD, long-lived API-key mint/list/revoke, user
  preferences, constitution CRUD.

Workflow definitions vs. run history (a deliberate split, D-02):

- [workflows.py](../../backend/app/api/workflows.py) -> `/api/workflows`: read-only, manifest-derived workflow *definitions*
  (`compile_for_run` + `get_pipeline_agents`) — no DB query.
- [runs.py](../../backend/app/api/runs.py) -> `/api/runs`: `WorkflowRun` history CRUD — list/get/delete, pptx export,
  chain-context, artifacts, events (legacy poll), family, summary, hook-runs, gate-events,
  validation-results, exec-runs. All IDOR-filtered on `user_id == current_user.id`.
- [user_workflows.py](../../backend/app/api/user_workflows.py) -> `/api/user-workflows`: saved (user-composed) workflow definitions —
  CRUD over `{base_pipeline_type, agent_ids, model_overrides}`, reusing the
  `WorkflowDefinition` table with `source="user"`. The row's `manifest_json` shape
  (absent vs. carrying a `"steps"` key) is what later decides, at launch, which of the
  three `LaunchSource` shapes this row becomes — see
  [DOMAIN-workflow-compilation.md](DOMAIN-workflow-compilation.md)'s "The three launch
  shapes" and [ADR-0020](../cards/20260824-1831-ADR-0020.md).

The run-transport cluster — six modules sharing the `/api/runs` prefix, split by concern
rather than merged into [runs.py](../../backend/app/api/runs.py):

- [run_engine.py](../../backend/app/api/run_engine.py) — no router; transport-neutral shared infra (per-run `asyncio.Queue`/
  task/cancel-event registries, image-ingress validators, JWT+DB helpers) that must outlive
  the retired `/ws/chat` endpoint. Imported by both the old WS path and the new REST/SSE
  endpoints.
- [run_stream.py](../../backend/app/api/run_stream.py) -> `GET /api/runs/{id}/events/stream`: the SSE down-channel. Stamps durable
  `seq` as the frame `id:` line (browser `Last-Event-ID` resume), replays the durable tail,
  emits `stream_attached`, and re-arms `review_gate_ready` on reattach if a gate is still open.
  `_STREAM_TERMINAL_TYPES` is the gate-resolution set minus `review_gate_approved`, UNIONED
  with `pipeline_diverted` — a divert ends the stream (spec 014 R-13) but is not a gate
  resolution, and that set also derives the re-arm vocabulary, so it is unioned rather than
  widened at the source.
- [run_commands.py](../../backend/app/api/run_commands.py) -> `POST /api/runs/{id}/gate|answers|cancel|resume|messages|revisions`,
  `POST /api/runs` (launch), `POST /api/runs/user_message`: the up-channel REST commands —
  thin wrappers over the *same* store seams (`set_review_response`,
  `set_questionnaire_responses`, cooperative cancel) the legacy WS handlers used. `POST
  /api/runs` detects which of three `LaunchSource` shapes it is handling — file-backed,
  a saved flat row, or a manifest tree (saved OR sent inline and compiled `trust="user"`,
  so an unsaved composition runs without being saved first) — see [ADR-0020](../cards/20260824-1831-ADR-0020.md).
  Largest file in the module.
- [chat_router.py](../../backend/app/api/chat_router.py) — no router; the mechanical (zero-model-call) intent classifier that
  decides which of `run_commands`'s four channels (answers/gate/steering/revision, plus a
  concierge escalation) a chat turn is dispatched on, keyed only on generic run-state
  signals — never a workflow name.
- [run_files.py](../../backend/app/api/run_files.py) -> `POST /api/runs/{id}/files`: owner-scoped document upload into the run's
  sandbox `.uploads/` prefix, with text-extraction sidecar for agent consumption.
- [run_shutdown.py](../../backend/app/api/run_shutdown.py) — no router; `shutdown_run_infrastructure()` called from [app/main.py](../../backend/app/main.py)'s
  lifespan shutdown to drain Concierge tasks, run-transport queues, then close the
  checkpointer, in that load-bearing order.

Composition/launch helpers (no routers — imported by [run_commands.py](../../backend/app/api/run_commands.py) / [user_workflows.py](../../backend/app/api/user_workflows.py)):

- [composition_order.py](../../backend/app/api/composition_order.py) — app-layer adapter over the kernel's `WorkflowResolver.presort`;
  reorders a user's agent composition producer-first (or rejects it) at compose time, before a
  `WorkflowRun` is minted.
- [launch_context.py](../../backend/app/api/launch_context.py) — resolves whether a launch loads OpenDesign template/design-system
  context, keyed on the manifest's declared `context_providers: [opendesign]` signal rather
  than a `pipeline_type` name-branch.

Agent/capability surfaces:

- [agents.py](../../backend/app/api/agents.py) -> `/api/agents`: pipeline agent listing, per-user skills CRUD, per-agent prompt
  read/write/delete.
- [capabilities.py](../../backend/app/api/capabilities.py) -> `/api/capabilities`: the hardened CapabilityRegistry palette
  (kind/name/user_allowed/description/security_gated) the frontend composer renders.

Chat and file surfaces:

- [chats.py](../../backend/app/api/chats.py) -> `/api/chats`: chat session CRUD + message append.
- [file_extract.py](../../backend/app/api/file_extract.py) -> `POST /api/files/extract-text`: PDF/DOCX/PPTX text extraction for
  workflow briefs (pypdf/python-docx/python-pptx), capped at [settings.BRIEF_MAX_CHARS](../../backend/app/api/settings.py).
- [analytics.py](../../backend/app/api/analytics.py) -> `GET /api/analytics/summary`: owner-scoped, read-only aggregation over the
  caller's own `WorkflowRun` rows (no new table/migration).

Template catalogues (read-only; generation happens through the pipeline, not these routers):

- [ppt_templates.py](../../backend/app/api/ppt_templates.py) -> `/api/ppt`: PPT/deck template catalogue.
- [prototype_templates.py](../../backend/app/api/prototype_templates.py) -> `/api/prototype`: prototype template + design-system catalogue.

External-integration cluster (`/flowin-handoff`, IDE-to-browser handoff):

- [install.py](../../backend/app/api/install.py) -> `/install`: serves the installer bash script (slash command + local capture
  script) as string constants — unauthenticated, no secrets.
- [handoff.py](../../backend/app/api/handoff.py) -> `/api/handoff`: `POST /receive` (IDE, API-key auth) creates a session;
  `GET /{token}` (browser, JWT) reads it; `POST /{token}/start` kicks the pipeline,
  fire-and-forget.
- [websocket_handoff.py](../../backend/app/api/websocket_handoff.py) -> `WS /ws/handoff/{token}`: the live event channel for a handoff run;
  in-memory single-process pub/sub (`_SUBSCRIBERS`), auth via `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` bearer
  subprotocol.
- [mcp.py](../../backend/app/api/mcp.py) -> `/mcp`: minimal remote MCP server (JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP-streamable POST)
  exposing a `flowin_handoff` tool; no GET/SSE side since there's nothing to push.

[__init__.py](../../backend/app/api/__init__.py) is a one-line package marker; no shared exports.

## Why this shape

- **Definitions vs. history split ([workflows.py](../../backend/app/api/workflows.py) vs. [runs.py](../../backend/app/api/runs.py), D-02)**: `/api/workflows`
  used to serve run-history CRUD; it was reclaimed for manifest-derived static definitions
  (needed by the composer) and the DB-backed run history moved wholesale to `/api/runs`, with
  no legacy redirect aliases — confirmed safe because those routes are JWT-only with no
  external API-key consumer.
- **SSE replaced `/ws/chat` (REQ-CHAT-07/D-13), and the replacement is deliberately fragmented,
  not folded into [runs.py](../../backend/app/api/runs.py)**: [run_stream.py](../../backend/app/api/run_stream.py) (down-channel firehose) and [run_commands.py](../../backend/app/api/run_commands.py)
  (up-channel REST commands: gate/answers/cancel/resume/messages/revisions/launch) are split
  because they're different transport directions with different lifecycles — one is a
  long-lived `text/event-stream` response, the other is a set of ordinary request/response
  POSTs. Both are kept thin wrappers over pre-existing store seams (`set_review_response`,
  `set_questionnaire_responses`, the cooperative cancel-event registry) specifically so no new
  event shape or persistence path was introduced during the cutover — the WS-era code paths
  were extracted-before-deleted ([run_engine.py](../../backend/app/api/run_engine.py)'s docstring cites this as "INV-12
  extract-before-delete").
- [run_engine.py](../../backend/app/api/run_engine.py) and [run_shutdown.py](../../backend/app/api/run_shutdown.py) are routerless "no-FastAPI-surface" modules within
  app.api: [run_engine.py](../../backend/app/api/run_engine.py) explicitly documents that it imports no FastAPI transport code so
  both the (now-retired) WS endpoint and the REST/SSE endpoints could resolve the same
  queue/cancel/validator symbols from one place during the migration. [run_shutdown.py](../../backend/app/api/run_shutdown.py) exists
  because the original lifespan shutdown was a bare log line — uvicorn's graceful-shutdown
  timeout doesn't close an in-flight SSE stream, so nothing ever reached real teardown;
  ordering (await Concierge tasks -> drain run-transport -> close checkpointer last) is
  load-bearing and documented inline.
- **Import boundary (ports-and-adapters)**: app.api is explicitly the *app* side of a
  kernel/app split — [run_engine.py](../../backend/app/api/run_engine.py)'s docstring states the engine kernel
  (`agents/execution_engine/`) never imports app.*, enforced by import-linter.
  [composition_order.py](../../backend/app/api/composition_order.py) and [launch_context.py](../../backend/app/api/launch_context.py) exist as app-layer adapters precisely so
  callers that must avoid a direct [agents.execution_engine](../../backend/app/api/agents.py) import (or a workflow-name
  literal) go through a boundary module instead of reimplementing kernel logic or branching on
  `pipeline_type` strings (the repeated "SC-001/INV-1: never branch on workflow name" pattern
  seen in [chat_router.py](../../backend/app/api/chat_router.py), [composition_order.py](../../backend/app/api/composition_order.py), and [launch_context.py](../../backend/app/api/launch_context.py)).
- [chat_router.py](../../backend/app/api/chat_router.py) is a pure classifier, not a handler: it lives in app.api (not the kernel)
  specifically so a banned-pattern import-linter gate over `agents/execution_engine/` stays
  green, and it does zero LLM/model calls — free-form turns it can't classify escalate to the
  Concierge, whose actual model invocation happens in [run_commands.post_message](../../backend/app/api/run_commands.py), keeping the
  routing decision itself cheap and deterministic.
- Template catalogues are read-only by design: [ppt_templates.py](../../backend/app/api/ppt_templates.py) and
  [prototype_templates.py](../../backend/app/api/prototype_templates.py) only serve catalogue metadata; generation is deferred to the
  pipeline (`od_ppt`/`od_prototype` workflows) so the frontend gallery can render
  before/independent of the agent build.
